text: GPT stands for generative pre-trained transformer. What does the transformer part refer to?
options: A neural network architecture based on attention
A chip designed for running neural networks
The database the model was trained on
The tokenizer that splits text into pieces
answer: A neural network architecture based on attention
explanation: The transformer is a family of network architectures built on the multi-head attention mechanism, published by Google in 2017. GPT is an instantiation of it, which is why the two terms get used interchangeably even though one is a building block and the other is a product line.

text: OpenAI released GPT-3 in 2020. Roughly how many parameters did it have?
explanation: 175 billion parameters, which was a hundred times larger than GPT-2 and made few shot prompting suddenly look like a new capability. It also produced the paper on emergent behaviour, the zero shot examples, that launched most of the prompt engineering discourse.

text: Google's Gemini family of models took its name partly from NASA's Project Gemini. Why?
options: Because the models run on lunar hardware
Because the models were trained on space imagery
Because the models are named after twins
Because the models replaced the Gemini constellation
answer: Because the models are named after twins
explanation: Gemini is Latin for twins, chosen to mark the merger of Google Brain and DeepMind, and it is also a nod to Project Gemini. Two unrelated reasons for one name is about usual for Google, and it is a good trick for asking what a model name is actually referring to.

text: Meta's Llama series expands its own name into a backronym. What does L stand for?
explanation: Large Language Model Meta AI, which is a backronym because Llama already existed as a word. The name was chosen partly because the animal is unlikely to be trademarked, and the release in February 2023 was the moment open weight models became genuinely competitive with the closed ones.

text: Stable Diffusion, released in 2022, generates images using which broad technique?
explanation: A diffusion model learns to reverse a process that destroys structure, so generation runs backwards from noise. Because that gives a much larger space to interpolate in, diffusion models largely displaced GANs for image generation within a couple of years of Stable Diffusion's release.

text: DALL-E, DALL-E 2 and DALL-E 3 are all text to image models from which company?
explanation: All three come from OpenAI, and the name is a homage to Salvador Dali with the hyphen changed to a middle dot. The confusing part is that Midjourney, Stability AI and Runway are all independent competitors doing the same job, so the four names on this list get confused constantly.

text: BERT differs from GPT in one architectural way that changed the field. What is it?
options: It is decoder only and generates text one token at a time
It is trained from scratch on raw unlabeled video
It is encoder only and reads text in both directions
It uses a mixture of experts to route each token
answer: It is encoder only and reads text in both directions
explanation: BERT masks tokens and predicts them from context on both sides, so it produces representations rather than continuations. That encoder only design is why BERT rewrote search and sentiment analysis overnight and why every later model describes itself as a BERT variant, for better or worse.

text: GPT-2 was pre-trained on a dataset of how many web pages?
explanation: 8 million pages, and the more interesting part is what happened next. OpenAI released a 124 million parameter version in February 2019 and held the 1.5 billion parameter one back until November, saying a model that good could be used to generate convincing fake text.

text: ChatGPT was first released on which date?
explanation: November 30, 2022, which is the date most people mean when they say generative AI went mainstream. It is usually credited with catalysing the AI boom, and the model underneath was a GPT-3.5 fine-tune, not a new frontier model.

text: AlphaGo Zero differed from earlier AlphaGo versions in one important way. What was it?
options: It ran on mobile hardware rather than servers
It learned entirely from self play with no human games
It played a different board size than its predecessors
It used a different search algorithm for the opening
answer: It learned entirely from self play with no human games
explanation: Earlier versions learned from human games, while AlphaGo Zero started from random play and reached superhuman strength on its own. The original AlphaGo was defeated by Lee Sedol in 2016 because of move 37, a move so strange that it had been dismissed as an error, and Zero then beat the version that beat him.

text: Which company released GPT-4 in March 2023?
explanation: OpenAI released GPT-4 on March 14, 2023 as a multimodal model accepting image and text input. Anthropic is the closest wrong answer because it released Claude the same month, but Claude is a different model family from a different lab.

text: Which model was the first widely released large reasoning model that thinks through a chain of thought before answering?
explanation: OpenAI released the o1-preview on September 12, 2024, resetting its counter to 1 for a new reasoning series trained to spend test-time compute thinking before responding. DeepSeek-R1 is the tempting wrong answer, but it arrived later in January 2025 and matched o1 rather than preceding it.

text: What made DeepSeek-R1 notable when it launched in January 2025?
options: Open weights with frontier-level math and code reasoning
Closed API-only video generation from text prompts
Tiny on-device model for keyboard autocomplete
answer: Open weights with frontier-level math and code reasoning
explanation: DeepSeek-R1 shipped under the MIT license in January 2025 and matched OpenAI o1 on math and code benchmarks despite far lower reported training cost. The video-generator distractor describes Sora-style models, not a reasoning language model, which is why it fails on the math and code hook.

text: What is Constitutional AI, the technique Anthropic introduced for training Claude?
options: Pretraining only on masked words in both directions
Routing each token through two of eight expert networks
Training guided by a written constitution of principles
Upscaling images by reversing a noise process
answer: Training guided by a written constitution of principles
explanation: Anthropic's December 2022 method trains a harmless assistant from a written constitution plus AI feedback (RLAIF) instead of human harm labels. The expert-routing distractor describes mixture-of-experts models like Mixtral, which is an architecture choice, not an alignment technique.

text: What made Meta's Llama 2 release in July 2023 significant compared with Llama 1?
options: It shipped as an API-only product with no downloadable weights
It generated minute-long video clips from text prompts
It was restricted to academic researchers on request
Its weights were released free for research and commercial use
answer: Its weights were released free for research and commercial use
explanation: Meta released Llama 2 on July 18, 2023 with weights available free for research and commercial use, unlike Llama 1 which was gated to researchers under a non-commercial license. The researcher-only distractor describes Llama 1 itself, which is exactly why it confuses people.

text: What architecture does Mistral's Mixtral 8x7B, released in December 2023, use?
options: Sparse mixture of experts with routed subnetworks
answer: Sparse mixture of experts with routed subnetworks
explanation: Mixtral 8x7B is a sparse mixture-of-experts decoder where a router sends each token to two of eight expert groups, giving 46.7B parameters at a fraction of the active cost. The diffusion distractor belongs to image generators like Stable Diffusion, not to this language model.

text: What does OpenAI's Sora, previewed in February 2024, generate?
options: Protein structures from amino acid sequences
Short video clips from text prompts
answer: Short video clips from text prompts
explanation: OpenAI previewed Sora on February 15, 2024 as a text-to-video model generating up-to-a-minute clips from written prompts. The speech-transcript distractor describes Whisper, OpenAI's audio model, which is why the two get mixed up.

text: Which model first offered a 1-million-token context window in February 2024?
explanation: Google's Gemini 1.5 Pro, announced February 15, 2024, ran up to 1 million tokens, then the longest context of any large-scale foundation model. GPT-4 Turbo is the tempting miss because its 128k window led at the time, but it was roughly an eighth of Gemini's reach.

text: Which company develops the Qwen family of language models?
explanation: Qwen, also called Tongyi Qianwen, is built by Alibaba Cloud, with its weights opening up from late 2023. Baidu is the natural confusion because its Ernie Bot is the other famous Chinese LLM, but Ernie and Qwen come from different companies.

text: Which company develops the Grok family of models?
explanation: Grok is built by xAI, the company Elon Musk launched in 2023, and debuted as a chatbot in November 2023 with live knowledge from X. OpenAI tempts people because Musk co-founded it, but he left years before Grok existed.

text: What does OpenAI's Whisper, released as open-source software in September 2022, do?
options: Transcribes and translates speech into text
Plays strategy games at superhuman level
answer: Transcribes and translates speech into text
explanation: Whisper is an encoder-decoder speech recognition model trained on 680,000 hours of audio that transcribes many languages and translates them into English. The image-generation distractor describes DALL-E, OpenAI's other famous model family of that era.

text: What does the "o" stand for in GPT-4o, released in May 2024?
explanation: The "o" stands for "omni", marking GPT-4o as natively multimodal across text, audio, and image in one network. "Open" is the trap because the maker is OpenAI, but the May 2024 announcement spells out omni.

text: Anthropic's assistant Claude was named after which computer scientist?
explanation: Anthropic named Claude after Claude Shannon, the founder of information theory. Alan Turing was a computing pioneer but has no connection to the name, despite being the tempting classic-computing answer.

text: The word Grok, used for xAI's chatbot, comes from which science fiction novel?
options: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
explanation: Grok was coined by Robert Heinlein in Stranger in a Strange Land, meaning to understand deeply. Neuromancer gave us cyberspace and feels similar, but it never used the word grok.

source.title: Stranger in a Strange Land

text: The name DALL-E combines artist Salvador Dali with which movie robot?
explanation: DALL-E is a portmanteau of Dali and WALL-E, the Pixar robot. EVE is tricky because she is from the same film, but she is not part of the name.

text: Google's chatbot Bard was renamed to what in 2024?
explanation: Google retired the Bard name and rebranded the chatbot as Gemini, matching its model family. ChatGPT is OpenAI's rival product, not a Google rename.

text: GitHub Copilot was built through a partnership between GitHub and which AI lab?
explanation: Copilot launched as a GitHub and OpenAI collaboration, powered by OpenAI's Codex models. GitHub and Google sounds plausible since Google makes coding tools, but Google was never the Copilot partner.

text: DeepMind's AlphaGo famously mastered which board game?
explanation: AlphaGo was built to play Go and beat world champion Lee Sedol in 2016. Chess is the trap because its sibling AlphaZero later mastered chess too, but AlphaGo itself played Go.

text: DeepMind's AlphaFold is famous for predicting what?
explanation: AlphaFold predicts the 3D shape of proteins from their amino acid sequences. Weather forecasts are the tempting pick because DeepMind also builds forecasting models, but that is GraphCast, not AlphaFold.

text: The ChatGPT product generates which of the following in response to a user prompt?
explanation: ChatGPT answers a prompt with text, speech and images from the same service, and it has been a freemium product since it launched on November 30, 2022. People assume it is a text-only tool because that is all it did for its first few months, which is the gap the later voice and image features closed.

text: What does the AI tool Midjourney generate?
explanation: Midjourney turns written prompts into images, and its open beta in July 2022 made it one of the best-known AI image generators. Writing code from plain English describes GitHub Copilot, a different kind of tool.

text: What does GitHub Copilot help programmers do?
explanation: Copilot lives inside code editors like Visual Studio Code and suggests whole lines and functions as you type; it was first announced in June 2021. Deploying apps and tracking bugs are GitHub platform features, not what the Copilot assistant itself does.

text: How did OpenAI release the Whisper speech recognition model in 2022?
options: As a cloud-only service with a fee
As a feature locked inside ChatGPT
As a paid app on mobile stores
explanation: OpenAI released Whisper's code and weights for anyone to download in September 2022, which is why it quickly turned up inside transcription apps and subtitle tools. The cloud-only distractor describes how OpenAI served models like DALL-E, not Whisper.

text: To make an image with OpenAI's DALL-E, what does the user provide?
options: A rough pencil sketch to trace over
A voice memo describing the scene
A written description of the image
answer: A written description of the image
explanation: DALL-E is a text-to-image model: you type a description, called a prompt, and it generates a matching picture. Sketch and audio inputs describe other tools; DALL-E's defining input has always been natural language text.

text: Claude, first released in March 2023, is what kind of product?
explanation: Claude is Anthropic's conversational AI, released as a chatbot in March 2023 and used for writing, analysis, and coding. A smart home speaker is hardware like Amazon's Echo, a different product category entirely.

text: What made Stable Diffusion's 2022 release unusual among image models at the time?
options: It could generate video as well as images
It was built by OpenAI as a DALL-E sequel
Its code and weights were released publicly
It was the first model to generate images
answer: Its code and weights were released publicly
explanation: Stability AI released Stable Diffusion's code and model weights publicly in 2022, a departure from DALL-E and Midjourney, which were reachable only through cloud services. That openness let anyone run it on a home GPU and turned it into the base for countless derivative image tools.
answerAliases: code and model weights have been released publicly

text: What style of interaction made ChatGPT famous when it launched?
options: One-word answers with no memory of context
Voice commands that control home devices
explanation: ChatGPT keeps the thread of a conversation, so a user can say 'make it shorter' and be understood; that follow-up-friendly chat carried it to 100 million users in two months. Voice assistants like Alexa already handled single commands, but they were not open-ended conversation partners.

text: Which Chinese technology company developed the chatbot Ernie Bot and the ERNIE models behind it?
explanation: Baidu built both the chatbot and the ERNIE model family underneath it, opening Ernie Bot to the public in August 2023 after Chinese regulators approved it. Alibaba is the tempting wrong answer because Qwen is the other well known Chinese model family, but Qwen and ERNIE come from different companies.

text: Google's Gemini family of models, announced in December 2023, directly succeeded which two earlier model lines?
explanation: Gemini replaced LaMDA, the conversational model behind Bard, and PaLM 2, the dense model behind the text-only Bard. Both were Google products that had already shipped publicly, which is why Gemini was framed as a consolidation rather than a first attempt.

text: Which country is the AI lab behind the DeepSeek R1 reasoning model based in?
explanation: DeepSeek is based in Hangzhou and funded by the High-Flyer hedge fund, which is unusual because its research money did not come from outside investors looking for a return. South Korea is the tempting wrong answer because it has its own model labs, but DeepSeek is Chinese.

text: Which model family did Meta release with downloadable weights in February 2023?
explanation: Llama landed in February 2023 with weights anyone could download, which is what turned open models from a research curiosity into the default choice for people building products. Gemma is the tempting wrong answer because Meta released that smaller family later, in 2024.

text: Which Go world champion did DeepMind's AlphaGo beat in the high-profile 2016 match?
explanation: AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol 4-1 in March 2016, and the second game produced move 37, a move so unfamiliar that commentators called it a mistake before it proved decisive. Ke Jie is the player AlphaGo beat later in 2017, so the two are the two most common confusions in this story.

text: Which company built AlphaGo, the Go-playing system that beat Lee Sedol in 2016?
explanation: DeepMind built AlphaGo in London, and Google's 2014 purchase of the company is why the win usually gets handed to Google. IBM's Deep Blue was the chess machine that beat Garry Kasparov in 1997, which is the version people misremember.

text: In which year did Stability AI release Stable Diffusion?
explanation: Stability AI released Stable Diffusion in August 2022 and published the weights, which meant anyone could generate images on their own machine for free. That openness is why it turned up inside so many apps and plugins within months.

text: What did Google put BERT to work on inside its own products?
explanation: Google released BERT in 2018 as a model for reading and understanding text, and it quickly improved how results were ranked in Google Search. Image and speech work belong to entirely different models: BERT reads, it does not generate.

text: The live voice demo of GPT-4o in May 2024 was compared to which film's talking operating system?
options: Blade Runner, the 1982 Ridley Scott film
A.I. Artificial Intelligence, the 2001 Spielberg film
explanation: Sam Altman's May 2024 demo opened with the line 'Hi, I'm GPT-4o', and the comparison people drew was the operating system in the 2013 Spike Jonze film Her. No robot rolled across the stage, which is part of why the clip landed the way it did.

text: ChatGPT launched in November 2022 and is often credited with making generative AI mainstream. What changed in public perception at that point?
options: Ordinary people could talk to a model without writing code or a prompt
OpenAI became the first lab to sell a chatbot
ChatGPT was free for everyone on day one
Every other lab paused work on chat models
answer: Ordinary people could talk to a model without writing code or a prompt
explanation: ChatGPT shipped a chat box in front of a GPT-3.5 model, so the barrier was the interface rather than the capability. Access was free, it was multilingual, and it kept the conversation going, which is why adoption was measured in months rather than the years that preceded it.

text: ELIZA, the 1960s program widely credited as the first chatbot, was written at which university?
explanation: Joseph Weizenbaum built ELIZA at MIT between 1964 and 1967, and it worked by pattern-matching user text and echoing it back as a question, which was enough to convince people it understood them. Weizenbaum was disturbed by that success and wrote a whole paper about how easy it is to fool people with a machine this simple.

text: How long did Microsoft's Tay chatbot stay online in 2016?
explanation: Tay launched on Twitter on March 23, 2016 and Microsoft pulled it 16 hours later after it had been fed racist messages by internet trolls and repeated them back. The name stood for Tay, an AI think-tank product, and the episode is the standard cautionary tale about what happens when a model trains on whatever people feed it.

text: Which company's question-answering system beat the reigning champions on the US quiz show Jeopardy! in 2011?
explanation: IBM Watson beat Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter on Jeopardy! in February 2011, and it was built as part of IBM's DeepQA project rather than as a consumer product. The name comes from Thomas J. Watson, IBM's founder, not from the company being good at anything in particular.

text: The chess computer Deep Blue became the first to beat a reigning world champion under standard time controls in which year?
explanation: Deep Blue beat Garry Kasparov in May 1997, and the rematch was billed as a rematch of the world champion defending his title. The machine started life at Carnegie Mellon as ChipTest, was renamed Deep Thought, and only became Deep Blue after moving to IBM, which is why the lineage is genuinely confusing.

text: Character.ai, the companion chatbot service launched in 2023, was designed by which pair of researchers?
options: Noam Shazeer and Daniel de Freitas
answer: Noam Shazeer and Daniel de Freitas
explanation: Noam Shazeer and Daniel de Freitas had already co-created LaMDA at Google before leaving to build Character.ai, so the two companies are directly linked in the chatbot timeline. Shazeer co-authored the transformer paper's attention work at Google Brain before that.
answerAliases: Noam Shazeer and Daniel de Freitas

text: What distinguishes Perplexity, the search startup founded in 2022, from a conventional search engine?
options: It ranks pages by how many other pages link to them
It searches a private index that no one outside the company can use
It answers with a written summary that cites its sources
It returns only images instead of text results
answer: It answers with a written summary that cites its sources
explanation: Perplexity processes a query and synthesizes a response from live web content while citing the pages it used, which is why it is called an answer engine rather than a link list. It was founded by former Google researchers and depends on other companies' models underneath, which is the part people find surprising.
answerAliases: answers with a written summary that cites its sources

text: What is Adobe Firefly, released in 2023, a family of models for?
options: Creative production work in design and media
Disease diagnosis from medical scan images
Fraud detection on bank transaction records
answer: Creative production work in design and media
explanation: Adobe Firefly is a web app and a family of generative models for creative production, covering text-to-image, text-to-video, speech, soundtrack and sound effects. It was trained on Adobe's own licensed stock library and public domain material so customers would not inherit the copyright exposure that hit earlier image generators.
answerAliases: Creative production work in design and media
family of generative artificial intelligence models for creative production

text: Replika, released in November 2017, builds each personal chatbot how?
options: By recording ten minutes of the user's speech
By uploading a photograph of the user's face
By importing the user's email history
By having the user answer a series of questions
answer: By having the user answer a series of questions
explanation: Replika is built by having the user answer a questionnaire that shapes the bot's own neural network, so each instance is customised rather than drawn from one shared model. Some users sued the company in 2023 after updates changed how the bot responded to them.
answerAliases: By having the user answer a series of questions
trained by having the user answer a series of questions

text: In the Markov chain model, what does the probability of each next event depend on?
options: Only the state of the immediately preceding event
The average of all previous probabilities
The single most likely event seen so far
Every event in the entire history
answer: Only the state of the immediately preceding event
explanation: The Markov assumption is that the future depends only on the present state, which is exactly what makes the math tractable. It is also the limiting idea behind early text generators that predicted the next word from the last few words, and behind much of the recommendation-engine work that predates modern models.
answerAliases: Only the state of the immediately preceding event
the state attained in the previous event
only the state of the previous event

text: DeepMind's MuZero learned chess, Go and shogi in 2019. How was it set up differently from AlphaGo and AlphaZero?
options: It was trained only on Atari games
It was built by a different research group
It was never told the rules of the games
It was given the rules but no board
answer: It was never told the rules of the games
explanation: MuZero receives only screen pixels and a win signal, so it has to learn the rules as well as the strategy, and it matched AlphaZero on Go, chess and shogi anyway. AlphaGo and AlphaZero were both handed explicit rule sets, which is the distinction that gets lost when the three are listed as one family of DeepMind systems.
answerAliases: It was never told the rules of the games

text: An autoencoder compresses its input into a smaller internal code. What is that code trained to do?
options: Rebuild the original input from the code
Pick which expert handles a token
Predict the next word in a sentence
answer: Rebuild the original input from the code
explanation: An autoencoder learns an encoding function and a decoding function, and the only way it can succeed at rebuilding its input is if the compressed code kept what mattered. That pressure to throw away noise is what makes the code useful for dimensionality reduction and embeddings, and image compression is the same idea with the decoder turned back into a real compressor.
answerAliases: Rebuild the original input from the code
a decoding function that recreates the input data

text: The Turing test asks a human evaluator to judge which of two things in a text conversation?
options: Which participant gave more accurate answers
Which participant is the human and which is the machine
Which participant used more complex vocabulary
answer: Which participant is the human and which is the machine
explanation: Alan Turing proposed the test in his 1950 paper as a way to replace the unanswerable question of whether machines can think with a behavioural one. The machine passes if the evaluator cannot reliably tell it apart from the human, which is why the test measures the illusion of understanding rather than understanding itself.
answerAliases: Which participant is the human and which is the machine
